text.p: Top-seeded defending champion Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands won a duel of big servers Thursday as she beat American Nicole Arendt 6-4 3-6 6-4 Thursday at the Bell Challenge.
The second-round match came down to one service break in each set.
"It's a fast surface and Nicole served well," said Schultz-McCarthy, who has the fastest serve in women's tennis. "Now I know how people feel when they have to return my serve."
Also advancing to Friday's quarter-finals was second-seeded Russian Elena Likhovtseva, a 6-2 5-7 6-2 winner over 117th-ranked American Katrina Adams.
The 24th-ranked Likhovtseva will now play unseeded American Jolene Watanabe, ranked 100th. Watanabe defeated Japanese qualifier Haruka Inoue 6-3 6-1.
Fourth seeded Kimberly Po also reached the quarters, outsteadying fellow-American Anne Miller from the baseline 6-2 3-6 6-0.
After breaking Arendt's serve in the fourth game of the match, the 11th-ranked Schultz-McCarthy was unable to take a game against her lefthanded opponent's serve until the final game of the match.
"I broke her in the first set and then after not doing anything on my serve she hit four winners to break me (in the sixth game) in the second," said Schultz-McCarthy. "I didn't expect that."
Schultz-McCarthy had a surprisingly easy break of serve herself in the last game on four quick points.
"When you play against a game like mine, that's when the pressure comes -- when you serve at 4-5 and you know you have to hold," she said.
The 25-year-old Schultz-McCarthy, who was supposed to play doubles with Gabriela Sabatini in upcoming events in Chicago and Philadelphia, had a few thoughts on her partner's retirement announcement.
"She's a great girl," Schultz-McCarthy said. "She just wasn't having any fun playing any more, so it was time to quit. It was heartbreaking seeing her on the court."
